trazo: Edit this approved hand-drawn, finely hatched editorial illustration. Only revise the woman's face; preserve the entire scene, clothing, crouching pose, hands, saucer, water, plants, barrel, textures, palette, lighting, 2:1 horizontal crop and overall head size. The art director now wants a complete face with CORRECT FACIAL ANATOMY, not an eyeless face. Redraw the facial features together as one coherent anatomical construction in the existing near-profile/three-quarter view, head inclined down and facing left toward the saucer. Establish one consistent tilted facial axis and perspective: the visible eye belongs naturally in its socket above and behind the nasal bridge; the nose projects from that bridge and connects naturally to the upper lip; the small closed mouth sits below the nose and above a proportionate chin. Give the face a believable forehead, cheek, jaw and philtrum with natural adult proportions. Subtle adjustment of nose and chin contours is allowed to make the anatomy coherent, but keep the same adult woman, head tilt, hairstyle and pose. Only show the far eye if the perspective really permits it; do not paste a frontal pair of eyes onto a profile. Her mouth should be readable again as in the reference, with the original warm terracotta contrast and a small relaxed closed-lip shape: do not erase it into skin, do not reduce it to an invisible line, no broad grin or visible teeth. Calm focused adult expression. Keep the same contour drawing, color wash and fine hatching as the source; do not switch styles. Do not simply add a separate eye on the blank face without reconstructing the relationships among eye, nose, mouth and chin. No text, frames, labels or collage.
